title: Twelve-hour safety sandbox + metric probe
body:
Purpose: quick, instrumented playtest plan to validate safety, latency, and cost signals in the first twelve hours of a limited pilot. Use this as the canonical checklist for the oncall + product-ops shift that covers 00:00–12:00 after soft-go. Keep decisions small: stop/revert thresholds are explicit and measurable.

Context and scope:
- Audience: small pilot cohorts (internal + 50 early customers). Not full rollout.
- Environment: dedicated capacity pool (pilot-dedicated-1) with canary routing to hosted fallback.
- Goal: detect safety regressions, latency regressions, and unexpected cost spikes quickly while keeping user experience intact.

Quick summary (TL;DR):
1) Validate safety signals on a 1% sampled traffic path with full logging. Stop if user-facing safe-fail rate > 1.5% on sampled queries or if auto-moderation false-negative rate increases by > 0.5 percentage points versus baseline.
2) Watch 95th latency and P99 token generation. If 95th latency degrades by > 250ms from baseline for more than 10m, shift traffic to fallback model variant.
3) Monitor token spend burn-rate; if minute-by-minute spend > 3x forecast for > 5m, pause non-critical traffic and reduce batch sizes.

Roles during the twelve-hour window:
- Safety lead: Sofia Patel — primary decision authority for content-related stops.
- Ops lead: Marcus Nguyen — capacity/fallback changes, autoscale tuning.
- Product oncall: Jonah Park — stakeholder comms and release flags.
- Observability engineer: Elena Rossi — dashboards and alert tuning.

Pre-flight checklist (complete before t0):
- [ ] Canary pool configured (pilot-dedicated-1) and smoke-tested with synthetic prompts (see JIRA-2319).
- [ ] Full request/response logging enabled for 1% sampled requests with KV cache tracing.
- [ ] Safety eval suite uploaded to Optimize (prompt set: pilot-safety-scan-v2).
- [ ] Baseline metrics snapshot taken and saved to /metrics/pilot-baselines/2025-11-04.
- [ ] Paging cadence set; oncall rotations confirmed for 0–12h window.
- [ ] Slack channel #pilot-12h-sandbox created and tied to severity webhook.

Metric probes and thresholds (automated watch + human checks):
- Safety signals:
  - auto-moderation false-negative rate (sampled) — baseline 0.3%; stop if > 0.8% sustained 10m.
  - user-exposed safety complaints (reports per 1k sessions) — alert if > 2 in 1h.
  - hallucination rate on structured outputs (detected via schema-checker) — notify if > baseline + 1.0pp.
- Performance signals:
  - 95th percentile latency (inference wall time) — baseline 420ms; throttle/fallback if > 670ms for >10m.
  - P99 token generation — baseline 920ms; if > 1.5x baseline for >5m, reduce batch window.
  - Error rate (5xx) — alert at >0.5% sustained 5m; immediate rollback at >1.5% sustained 3m.
- Cost signals:
  - per-minute token spend burn-rate vs expected (pilot forecast) — pause non-critical routes at >3x for >5m.
  - GPU memory pressure (percent of usable memory free) — autoscale if free < 12% for >2m.

Operational playbook (ordered actions)
- Safety alert triggered (auto-moderation false-neg > threshold):
  1) Safety lead posts summary to #pilot-12h-sandbox and triggers safety freeze flag.
  2) Redirect sampled traffic to hosted fallback model variant (fallback-safe-v1) within 2 minutes.
  3) Run full safety eval on the last 2k sampled requests; annotate examples and open JIRA-2320 if noise > 0.
- Latency regression (95th > threshold):
  1) Ops lead inspects batching window and KV cache hit-rate. If KV cache miss increased >10pp, flush and rebuild caches; if no change, reduce batch window by 30%.
  2) If change does not recover within 10m, shift canary traffic to lower-cost lower-latency model variant (latency-slim-1).
- Cost surge (>3x burn):
  1) Pause background/analytics routes and non-customer traffic.
  2) Decrease maximum batch size and disable aggressive prefetching for 10m.
  3) If spend remains high, scale down non-critical GPU pool nodes.

Mini-experiments to run (10–60 minute probes)
- Probe A: batch-size sensitivity — run 10m blocks at batch sizes [8, 16, 32], measure token/sec and 95th latency.
- Probe B: quantization toggle — test quantized-8 vs fp16 on a 5% traffic replica for 20m and compare output similarity (embedding cosine and BLEU for structured outputs).
- Probe C: prefix cache warmup — synthetic burst to prepopulate KV cache, measure hit-rate uplift 15m afterward.

Dashboard and alerts (obs tasks)
- Elena to publish a single-page dashboard (Pilot-12h-Safety-Probe) with: safety rate, 95th latency, P99 generation, per-minute burn, KV cache hit-rate, queue depth, 5xx rate.
- Alerts: set to 1-min evaluation windows for high-sensitivity signals (safety + 5xx), 5-min windows for latency/cost. Pager to product-oncall and ops (rotation list).

Communications template (short messages)
- Channel: #pilot-12h-sandbox (internal). Mention format: [SEV][time][metric] short sentence + top-line action.
- Customer comms (for the 50 early customers): short email template ready in /templates/pilot-customer-comms.md; product oncall to send only if we trigger a broad fallback > 30m.

Data collection & postmortem inputs (what to save)
- Save full sampled logs (1%) to secure S3 path with retention 90d.
- Export dashboard timeseries and experiment blocks as CSV and attach to JIRA-2320 if any threshold breach.
- Postmortem checklist: root cause, timeline, actions, owners, and regression test added to Optimize.

Decision heuristics (quick checks to avoid oscillation)
- Do not flip model variants more than once per 10 minutes.
- Only escalate to execs if multiple stop conditions hit within 60 minutes.
- Prefer targeted traffic routing (by customer cohort) rather than global pause unless severity is high.

Appendix: quick links and commands
- Telemetry dashboard (internal): https://obs.redwood.ai/d/pilot-12h-safety-probe
- Run synthetic smoke: gcloud run trigger --job=pilot-smoke --env=pilot-dedicated-1
- Canary traffic route toggle: POST /api/route-switch?pool=pilot-dedicated-1&target=fallback-safe-v1 (ops console)
- Baseline metrics CSV path: s3://redwood-prodops/pilot-baselines/2025-11-04/baselines.csv

Notes & unresolved questions (working):
- How to incorporate human review latency into safety threshold calculations — manual estimation needed from trust team.
- Do we want an automated short-circuit that pauses all traffic at a single safety metric breach? Current draft favors human-in-the-loop.
- Need final signoff from legal on the customer-facing short email template before t0.

Next steps before publish:
- Elena: dashboard and 1-min alert rules (due 2025-11-08).
- Marcus: verify autoscale policies and test failover script in staging (due 2025-11-06).
- Sofia: run safety eval sweep against pilot-safety-scan-v2 (due 2025-11-05).
- Jonah: prepare staff rotation roster and comms templates (due 2025-11-04).

Revision history:
- 2025-11-04: Draft created by Ava Martinez (initial checklist).
- 2025-11-10: Added probe experiments and cost thresholds (Elena).
- 2026-02-15: Clarified stop thresholds and added fallback API link (Marcus).
